title: CLI playground emulator: SDK rapid lab journal
body:
Purpose
This is a lab-style, messy journal exploring a small-footprint CLI-based playground (the emulator) for SDK onboarding and rapid prototyping. The emulator is intended to let engineers iterate on SDK integration, prompting patterns, and telemetry without spinning up a full cluster or using hosted credits.

Why this exists (motivation)
- Onramp friction: new integrators often get stuck on env setup or network config before they can try the API semantics.
- Fast feedback: want a 60–120s turnaround from change -> observation.
- Safety: keep experiments local (no secrets in public sandboxes), but produce realistic token/latency traces that look like hosted usage.

High-level idea
- CLI tool (play) that spins a containerized lightweight emulator (single process) + a local proxy that mimics Redwood routing rules (region/capacity fallback), plus a mock model backend that returns configurable latencies and token patterns.
- Hooks for telemetry capture (local file + optional forwarded stub to our telemetry test endpoint).
- Feature toggles: streaming vs chunked, kv-cache warm/cold, token limit enforcement, quantized-model behavior (emulated).

Quickstart (dev loop)
Prereqs:
- Docker or Podman installed
- Node 18+ (play CLI is JS for rapid iteration)
- Optional: local Linux kernel w/ user namespaces for rootless containers

Commands (prototype):
1) clone repo and start playground
   git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-playground.git && cd sdk-playground/emulator
   npm ci
   ./bin/play dev --config examples/basic.yaml

What ./bin/play does (dev):
- builds the mock image (if needed), starts a local proxy at http://localhost:31337, and prints a tiny connection token to stdout.
- writes telemetry to ./playground-logs/latest.log (rotating).

2) run the sample SDK script against emulator
   export REDWOOD_API_HOST=http://localhost:31337
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=play-test-token
   node examples/sample-chat.js

Expected output
- sample-chat.js shows streaming tokens, then app logs a latency report similar to: "request=chat-1 latency=172ms tokens=84 model=emul-7b-preview"
- playground-logs/latest.log contains JSONL lines with fields: ts, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, route_policy_applied

Telemetry contract (local)
- minimal JSONL schema (one line per request):
  { ts: "2026-02-18T15:02:23Z", request_id: "r-123", route: "hosted-default", model: "emul-7b-preview", tokens_in: 12, tokens_out: 84, latency_ms: 172, flags: ["streaming"] }
- Keep this intentionally tiny so we can easily diff logs across experiments.

Developer flows to validate
- Onboard flow: fresh repo -> install -> run example-chat -> see first streaming response within 90s.
- Failure recovery: drop the proxy (simulate network blip) and verify SDK retries/backoff are visible to the dev via clear CLI output.
- Cost simulation: emulator can surface token counting and a synthetic cost line (per-token cost config) so teams can prototype cost-limited UX.

Experiment matrix (short notes)
- Streaming chunk sizes: 8/16/32 tokens: measure perceived latency and number of flushes.
- KV cache warm vs cold: emulate a session with short prefixes and watch response delta.
- Fallback policy tests: configure proxy to prefer dedicated (higher-cost, low-latency emulation) then force capacity shortage to trigger fallback to hosted-sim. Observe SDK's route selection telemetry.

Sample session transcript (for onboarding docs)
- dev: ./bin/play dev --config examples/minimal.yaml
- play: "started proxy http://localhost:31337 • token=play-dev-7 • logs=./playground-logs/latest.log"
- dev: node examples/qa-bot.js
- bot: "...stream: Hello — how can I help?"
- dev: open ./playground-logs/latest.log -> see 3 entries (init, kv-warm, response)

Failure test recipes (quick checklist)
- Simulated OOM: set model.max_tokens=8 and send a 4k prompt; emulator returns 429 or truncated response. Verify SDK surfaces error category (quota vs model-error).
- Proxy auth fail: start with bad token -> expect SDK error and clear guidance text to the dev.
- Introduce 2000ms extra latency in emulator -> check client-side timeout heuristics and suggestions in sample readme.

Observability + UX cues
- Playground CLI prints a one-line human summary for each request: status, latency, token delta, cost estimate. This is the primary UX for fast debugging.
- The log file is machine-friendly for test harnesses. We should include a tiny CLI tail helper: ./bin/play tail --follow to show structured diffs.

Telemetry experiments we want to run
- Compare local emulator logs to hosted sandbox logs for 20 sample prompts to calibrate synthetic latencies.
- Test token counting parity: ensure emulator tokenization approximates our production tokenizer (not exact but close). If diverges >10% we add a warning to the README.

Open questions / notes to self
- Security: do we allow local encrypted KMS integration for folks testing private deployments? probably opt-in, documented.
- Should the CLI include a small web UI for non-engineer product folks? lightweight: static HTML + WS proxied by the CLI. Keep out of scope for first pass.
- How realistic should model stochasticity be? Might add deterministic seed option for evalability.

Next milestones (short, prioritised)
- P0: Keep the start-up flow <90s, ensure sample chat prints streaming tokens. (owner: Clara; ETA: 2 sprints)
- P1: Add basic route-policy emulation and static cost outputs. (owner: Ben; ETA: 3 sprints)
- P2: Add optional telemetry forwarder to staging telemetry endpoint for automated regression tests. (owner: Priya; ETA: 4 sprints)

Notes for docs page (what to include in public quickstart)
- one-liner: "Launch a local Redwood emulator for fast SDK prototyping (no cloud creds)."
- 3 commands: install, start, sample-run
- troubleshooting: top-5 errors (port in use, docker missing, bad token, proxy start fail, sample timeouts)
- short FAQ: "Can I use this to test private deployments?" -> basic guidance and warning about parity.

Loose TODOs / backlog items
- add a small fixture for streaming rate-limiting to mimic metered streaming stalls
- add an easy toggle to switch tokenizer models (approx-bpe vs exact)
- write a short internal video (5min) showing the dev loop for new hires
- investigate packaging play as a single binary (pkg/nx) to avoid node install friction

End of notes — this is intentionally raw. Use as source material for a cleaned-up PRD or quickstart README.

Unresolved: link to UI mockups and whether we keep the telemetry schema stable across versions (if not, include version field in JSONL).
